agent_notes: The superscription is verse 1 in the Hebrew numbering (KJV 44:0). 'Maskil' is left untranslated in the literal layer; its sense ('instruction', 'skilful poem') is disputed, and STEPBible's 'a poem' is only one guess. The Targum reads it as 'good instruction'.

lamnatzeach: STEPBible 'to the choirmaster' follows the usual reading of the piel participle of nātsach. I keep 'to the leader' in the literal layer, closer to the root's sense of 'to be preeminent/to oversee' (cf. YLT 'Overseer').

history.note: [consider] Consider '42, 44–49, 84–85, 87–88' (Psalm 43 is usually read with 42). (PS.44.1: "לִבְנֵי־קֹרַח" (the superscription formula that Psalm 43 lacks).)

agent_notes: 'af' at the head of the verse: I read it as a strong turn, 'yet/even so' (Ibn Ezra: 'not enough that you did not save us, but you rejected us'). Rashi reads it concessively ('even if you shame us, we will still praise your name'). The KJV 'But' is acceptable; I chose 'Yet'.

tashivenu achor (you make us turn backward) is imperfect, a continuing state; Rashi on Ps 44:11 notes it is present tense. I render it 'you make us turn back', not 'you have made'. Likewise shasu lamo is perfect, a completed act: 'have plundered for themselves'.

history.note: [consider] Consider changing root to שסה, or naming both (שסה/שסס) with Radak's view. (PS.44.11: lemma שָׁסָה H8154; Radak: "שסו למו. כמו המה שוסים מנחי הלמ"ד".)

agent_notes: Rashi's 'efandishnosh' (Old French, 'scatterings/dispersals') glosses zeritanu. I cite it only as Rashi's gloss, not as a claim I can check.

The Hebrew has no object after 'you did not increase'; Radak supplies 'your wealth' (לא הרביתה הונך) and Metzudat David reads 'you did not take great wealth in exchange'. The literal layer brackets 'your wealth' rather than choosing; the five English versions all supply it. STEPBible glosses the verb as a perfect ('you have sold') for an imperfect form; I glossed it as a present/habitual.

agent_notes: Malbim source corrected from 44:18 to 44:19, as requested. Malbim's reading (the steps did turn aside under exile, the heart did not) is kept as the minority view; the majority reading (the negative serves both clauses) is followed.

agent_notes: כִּי is read as 'though/even when' by Rashi, Meiri and Metzudat David, and as 'for' by Radak's more causal reading; the KJV, ASV and Webster take 'though'. The literal layer keeps 'for'; the dramatic layer carries the concessive sense. תנים: KJV 'dragons' is a mistranslation of 'jackals' (cf. תנין, sea monster, which Ibn Ezra's sea reading leans on); I could not confirm the Ibn Ezra reading beyond the packet's text.

agent_notes: Verse numbered as in the Hebrew (KJV 44:24). The Hebrew has no 'and' before 'forget': the two verbs stand side by side (asyndeton), as the questions of a protest do; the KJV and ASV supply 'and'. The final word ולחצנו is glossed 'and our oppression' with the conjunction attached to the noun.
Targum renders 'hide your face' as removing the Shekhinah of your glory; I cite it only as a softening of the anthropomorphism, which is its evident point.

STEPBible glosses שחה as 'it has sunk down' and BDB lists שׁוּחַ 'sink down'. The KJV 'bowed down' follows the sense of שׁחח (bow); both senses yield the same image. I kept 'has sunk down' in the literal layer. For בטננו the five versions split: 'belly' (KJV, YLT, Webster) against 'body' (ASV, BBE). I keep 'belly' in the literal layer, since the raw bodily word is the point, and note Ibn Ezra's reading of it as the body.
Stress claim corrected to the last syllable (milra), citing Radak; the 'fine, but' typo fixed. The other verses of the window are LOCKED or unchanged and are left out of this fragment.

agent_notes: Token 8 vatsheleichem (and you sent them away): STEPBible has 'set free'. In context the object is the nations, so I corrected it to 'sent them away', following Ibn Ezra ('as in vatgareshem') and Metzudat David. Radak and Meiri record a view that it means 'killed' (via Job 36:12); I did not adopt it.

The subject of vatitaem (planted them) and its referent are not marked: the suffix returns to the fathers, not the nations (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri). English versions split here (BBE adds 'our fathers'; ASV keeps 'them'). I bracket 'our fathers' in the literal layer.
Revised after the reviewer's request: the commentary no longer says the KJV adds 'by'. The KJV additions named are 'own' (twice) and 'in possession'. PS.44.5 is LOCKED and left out of this fragment.

רְצִיתָם: STEPBible gives 'you took pleasure in them'; I kept that sense ('you delighted in them'). Meiri offers a second reading from והרצת (Lev 26:34 in the usual numbering; the packet prints his citation as Lev 27:34), 'you made them whole', which I mention only through his name and do not adopt.

agent_notes: Sources corrected to Psalm 44:6 (Hebrew numbering; KJV 44:5). The imperfects נְנַגֵּחַ and נָבוּס can be read as habitual ('we gore') or as a wish or future ('we will gore'); the literal layer uses the plain present, the dramatic layer lets it sound like a boast of what always happens.
קָמֵינוּ is a participle ('those rising up against us'); Radak on this verse explains it as the same as צרינו. I did not cite Ibn Ezra's reading beyond what the packet gives.

agent_notes: Verse 6 moves from 'we' to 'I' (my bow, my sword). Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as the nation speaking as one, or the king/warrior for the whole; I keep the singular in all layers and explain it in the commentary.

hilalnu: STEPBible 'we have boasted' is right (piel of halal, 'to praise, to boast'); KJV 'we boast' is fine, but ASV/BBE soften or paraphrase to 'made our boast'/'our pride is in God'. I keep the boasting sense in the literal layer.
